extracted.intended_audience: securities exchanges, ETF sponsors, market lawyers/registrants, and interested public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and required disclosures/controls for an exchange proposed rule change to list and trade Commodity‑Based Trust Shares (a Spot Ether ETP) under BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4), including the SEC's legal standards and operational/structural requirements. Covers surveillance, custody, trust structure, creation/redemption, and disclosure/registration expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must determine that the proposal is consistent with the requirements of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, specifically including: (i) that a national securities exchange's rules are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices; and (ii) that an exchange proposal is designed, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing exchanges must explain how the proposal satisfies Section 6(b)(5). The Exchange argues that investor protection benefits (e.g., reduced premium/discount volatility, lower management fees, alternatives to risky custody) can outweigh or mitigate manipulation concerns; the Commission places the burden on the listing exchange to demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive surveillance‑sharing agreement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For Commodity‑Based Trust Shares, an exchange must demonstrate that there is a comprehensive surveillance‑sharing agreement in place with a regulated market of significant size related to the underlying commodity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hallmarks include sharing information about market trading activity, clearing activity, and customer identity; reasonable ability to obtain and produce requested information; and lack of rules/laws that would impede production. Joint membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group (ISG) has been treated historically as satisfying this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulated market of significant size test
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'market of significant size' is one where: (a) there is a reasonable likelihood that a person attempting to manipulate the ETP would also have to trade on that market to manipulate the ETP (so that surveillance-sharing would assist detection); and (b) it is unlikely that trading in the ETP would be the predominant influence on prices in that market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges must provide facts and analysis (e.g., futures market metrics, trading volumes, open interest, correlation measures) showing these two elements are satisfied with respect to the referenced regulated market (here, CME Ether Futures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable reliance on 'other means' to prevent manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will consider whether 'other means to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices' are sufficient to dispense with the requisite surveillance‑sharing agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges may argue that features such as geographically diverse spot markets, fragmentation with arbitrageurs, maturity and liquidity of futures markets, surveillance by regulated futures markets, and economic analyses demonstrating low ability to manipulate provide adequate protections. Such 'other means' must be demonstrated and justified in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of high correlation between futures and spot markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor/exchange should provide analysis showing that the regulated futures market (e.g., CME Ether Futures) is highly correlated with the spot market for the underlying commodity (ETH), so surveillance of the futures market would capture manipulative impacts on spot pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative correlation analyses (e.g., pairwise correlation of daily returns across spot platforms and CME futures over a defined period). Example: Sponsor's analysis showed daily correlation between spot ETH and CME Ether Futures of over 99.89% for Jan 1, 2022–Feb 1, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predominant influence/market impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The exchange must show that trading in the Shares would not be the predominant force on prices in the referenced regulated market (e.g., CME Ether Futures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use market metrics (spot 24‑hour trading volume, futures open interest, projected Trust assets/flows) to demonstrate the Trust would represent a very small percentage of market volume, and therefore could not predominate price formation. Courts have relied on relative market depth/liquidity comparisons in similar contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/structural assurances for custody
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust must adopt custodial arrangements and controls to mitigate risks of theft, loss, or unauthorized use of private keys and to protect investors from custodian insolvency or fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable measures include a regulated custodian (e.g., a New York chartered trust company subject to NYDFS oversight), segregation of Trust assets in accounts identifying the Trust as owner (bankruptcy‑remote treatment), fidelity insurance covering assets, and written policies/procedures consistent with industry best practices to demonstrate exclusive possession/control of digital assets. Sponsor argues these arrangements mitigate custody concerns cited by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on earning additional ETH / staking and treatment of incidental rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust, Sponsor, Custodian, and related persons must not engage in actions where any portion of the Trust's ETH becomes subject to proof‑of‑stake validation or is used to earn additional ETH or generate income; the Trust will disclaim and not account for incidental rights (e.g., forks or airdrops) in NAV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions are structural safeguards to prevent unintended exposure/complexity and to clarify NAV computation. Disclaimed assets are not included when determining NAV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and redemption procedures (cash on creation/redemption)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust will create and redeem Shares in cash transactions in baskets (example: Creation Basket of 10,000 Shares) at the Trust's NAV; authorized participants deliver cash to the Trust's account with the Cash Custodian in exchange for Shares, and the Trust delivers cash on redemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Transfer Agent facilitates settlement of creation/redemption orders. Except for sales of ether to cover Trust expenses, the Trust's ether moves only in connection with creations or redemptions, typically via third parties purchasing/delivering ether on behalf of the Trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust asset composition and cash equivalents standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust's assets shall consist only of ether, cash, or cash and cash equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cash equivalents are defined as short‑term instruments with maturities of less than three months. Any permanent change to NAV calculation methodology requires an exchange rule filing under Rule 19b‑4; ad hoc alternatives may be used only on an ad hoc basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of regulated, established service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust should appoint reputable, regulated entities to key roles (trustee, administrator, transfer agent, marketing agent, sub‑adviser, custodian, cash custodian) and document their responsibilities and contractual protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing names specific providers (e.g., Delaware Trust Company as trustee; Bank of New York Mellon as administrator/cash custodian; Coinbase Custody Trust Company as Custodian). The filing should describe how these arrangements contribute to investor protections (e.g., custody agreements, segregation, regulatory oversight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and registration requirements (Form S‑1 and availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Shares must be registered with the Commission via a registration statement (e.g., Form S‑1) and related descriptions of the Trust, Shares, and Index should be based on that registration statement; the Registration Statement must be effective before trading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registration statement should be filed and made available at prescribed locations (exchange website, Office of the Secretary, Commission's Public Reference Room). The filing notes the Registration Statement was not yet effective and the Shares will not trade until effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance‑sharing agreement hallmarks (detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: A surveillance‑sharing agreement should provide for sharing of information about market trading activity, clearing activity, and customer identity; parties must have reasonable ability to obtain and produce requested information; and no rules/laws/practices should impede information exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission has historically held that joint membership in the ISG constitutes such a surveillance‑sharing agreement. The surveillance sharing agreement is essential because it facilitates investigations and deters manipulation in derivative securities products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued listing representations and ongoing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange's 'Continued Listing Representations' regarding the Trust will constitute continued listing requirements for the Shares listed on the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing must set forth ongoing representations and the Exchange must monitor continued compliance with listing and operational requirements; failure to meet continued listing representations could affect listing status.
